cases.sentence: Степан Аркадьич с тем несколько ___, с которым он садился в председательское кресло в своем присутствии, вошел в кабинет Алексея Александровича.
cases.explain: «торжественным лицом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevitch, with the same somewhat solemn expression with which he used to take his presidential chair at his board, walked into Alexey Alexandrovitch’s room. Alexey Alexandrovitch was walking about his room with his hands behind his back, thinking of just what Stepan Arkadyevitch had been discussing with his wife.

cases.sentence: Чтобы скрыть это смущение, он достал только что купленную с ___ открывания папиросницу и, понюхав кожу, достал папироску.
cases.explain: «новым способом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I’m not interrupting you?” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, on the sight of his brother-in-law becoming suddenly aware of a sense of embarrassment unusual with him. To conceal this embarrassment he took out a cigarette case he had just bought that opened in a new way, and sniffing the leather, took a cigarette out of it.

cases.sentence: Алексей Александрович остановился и ничего не отвечал, но лицо его поразило Степана Аркадьича бывшим на нем выражением ___.
cases.explain: «покорной жертвы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Alexey Alexandrovitch stood still and said nothing, but his face struck Stepan Arkadyevitch by its expression of an unresisting sacrifice.

cases.sentence: Степан Аркадьич взял письмо, с недоумевающим удивлением посмотрел на ___, неподвижно остановившиеся на нем, и стал читать.
cases.explain: «тусклые глаза» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevitch took the letter, looked with incredulous surprise at the lusterless eyes fixed so immovably on him, and began to read.

cases.sentence: Молчание это было им обоим так неловко, что в губах Степана Аркадьича произошло ___ в то время, как он молчал, не спуская глаз с лица Каренина.
cases.explain: «болезненное содрогание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevitch handed back the letter, and with the same surprise continued looking at his brother-in-law, not knowing what to say. This silence was so awkward for both of them that Stepan Arkadyevitch’s lips began twitching nervously, while he still gazed without speaking at Karenin’s face.

cases.sentence: – Следовательно, ты находишь, что его нужно прекратить? – перебил его Алексей Александрович. – Но как? – прибавил он, сделав ___ руками пред глазами, – не вижу никакого возможного выхода.
cases.explain: «непривычный жест» — after the preposition «пред», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “So you consider it must be ended?” Alexey Alexandrovitch interrupted him. “But how?” he added, with a gesture of his hands before his eyes not usual with him. “I see no possible way out of it.”

cases.sentence: Если ты убедишься теперь, что вы не можете сделать ___…
cases.explain: «взаимного счастия» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “There is some way of getting out of every position,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, standing up and becoming more cheerful. “There was a time when you thought of breaking off. … If you are convinced now that you cannot make each other happy. …”

cases.sentence: ___ была так убедительна, что невольно Алексей Александрович, чувствуя свою слабость и подчиняясь ей, готов был верить тому, что скажет Степан Аркадьич. – Она никогда не выскажет этого.
cases.explain: «Добрая улыбка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “If you care to know my opinion,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch with the same smile of softening, almond-oil tenderness with which he had been talking to Anna. His kindly smile was so winning that Alexey Alexandrovitch, feeling his own weakness and unconsciously swayed by it, was ready to believe what Stepan Arkadyevitch was saying. “She will never speak out about it. But one thing is possible, one thing she might desire,” he went on, “that is the cessation of your relations and all memories associated with them. To my thinking, in your position what’s essential is the formation of a new attitude to one another. And that can only rest on a basis of freedom on both sides.”

cases.sentence: По-моему, в вашем положении необходимо уяснение новых ___.
cases.explain: «взаимных отношений» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “If you care to know my opinion,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch with the same smile of softening, almond-oil tenderness with which he had been talking to Anna. His kindly smile was so winning that Alexey Alexandrovitch, feeling his own weakness and unconsciously swayed by it, was ready to believe what Stepan Arkadyevitch was saying. “She will never speak out about it. But one thing is possible, one thing she might desire,” he went on, “that is the cessation of your relations and all memories associated with them. To my thinking, in your position what’s essential is the formation of a new attitude to one another. And that can only rest on a basis of freedom on both sides.”

cases.sentence: Да, развод, – краснея, повторил Степан Аркадьич. – Это во всех отношениях самый ___ для супругов, находящихся в таких отношениях, как вы.
cases.explain: «разумный выход» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, I imagine that divorce—yes, divorce,” Stepan Arkadyevitch repeated, reddening. “That is from every point of view the most rational course for married people who find themselves in the position you are in. What can be done if married people find that life is impossible for them together? That may always happen.” Alexey Alexandrovitch sighed heavily and closed his eyes.

cases.sentence: Это всегда может случиться. – Алексей Александрович тяжело вздохнул и закрыл глаза. – Тут только одно соображение: – желает ли один из супругов вступить в ___?
cases.explain: «другой брак» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, I imagine that divorce—yes, divorce,” Stepan Arkadyevitch repeated, reddening. “That is from every point of view the most rational course for married people who find themselves in the position you are in. What can be done if married people find that life is impossible for them together? That may always happen.” Alexey Alexandrovitch sighed heavily and closed his eyes.
